summary: 1951 cooperative lookout on a Six Rivers NF ridge, one of six late 809R towers the register counts; staffed in fire season, and the ridge's radio site is being relocated.

facts.design: Late-style 809R enclosed tower, 30 ft to the cab floor; the register says only six such towers exist

access.note: The register says the site is accessible to the public, about 6 miles from the nearest paved road. Staffed in fire season. No source confirms the cab can be climbed.

visit.trail_note: About 6 miles from the nearest paved road per the register; no route or trail is described.

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, Humboldt-Del Norte Unit (Cal Fire HUU)

events.note: First cooperative lookout in the Humboldt-Del Norte area, reported October 19, 1951; five companies and the Forest Service shared the costs
Vandals stripped the cab windows of glass (Humboldt Standard, May 3, 1954); damage put at $250; four young men arrested and confessed
Permit for state communications facilities on the site expires December 31, 2022; state facilities must be removed then (NPS release dated December 29, 2017)
State budget request (FY 2025-26) to relocate the Red Mountain communications site

notes_for_editor: The register's staffing line is undated; as_of is the date it was read. The register registration date and build year are consistent with the 1951 newspaper item. Nothing in the sources says whether the cab survives the communications relocation; the NPS release (dated December 29, 2017, archived) is not an updated source, and its 2022 permit expiry is not confirmed as carried out. The story first said 2018 for that release; the release date is December 2017. Access is recorded as public from the register; climbing is not confirmed, so the story does not encourage it. Photos not recorded: the register lists three photo credits (Osborne Fire-Finder, Sunset View, 2009 by Ron Kemnow) but I found no image URLs. The YouTube link in the record returned no page content.
